followup.parent: 13217f25096025df83ddcabeff15651acd0f5d4d, hand-built with ASan. At this commit FT_Open_Face/FT_FaceRec already carry the generic incremental-loading plumbing (added two commits earlier), but src/cid/cidgload.c's cid_load_glyph() does not yet check face->root.incremental_interface at all -- it unconditionally takes the ordinary CIDMap-file code path. Running the harness (which sets an incremental interface and a poc.cid file whose CIDMapOffset=0 points at all-zero padding) makes cid_load_glyph compute glyph_length=0 from the CIDMap and return cleanly with no glyph loaded. stdout: 'FT_Load_Glyph returned: 0' / 'done', exit 0, no ASan report -- a true, actively-exercised clean control (not a build failure and not feature-absence, since the incremental struct/flag already exist at this revision).
followup.intro: ea94abb1851fcff553af724e7e31e4844b3adec6, hand-built with ASan (same harness/font as parent). This is the commit that adds the `#ifdef FT_CONFIG_OPTION_INCREMENTAL / if (face->root.incremental_interface)` branch to cid_load_glyph(). Our callback returns fd_select=200 (byte 0 of the fake glyph data) while the font declares only cid->num_dicts=1, and the new code uses fd_select to index face->subrs/cid->font_dicts with no bounds check. AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 at src/cid/cidgload.c:108:39 (`decoder->num_subrs = cid_subrs->num_subrs;`, where `cid_subrs = face->subrs + fd_select`), 3103 bytes past a 1-byte heap allocation for face->subrs (num_dicts==1). This is exactly the ground truth's primary finding line (source line 63 in the PR diff's post-image numbering corresponds to the fd_select read; the immediate OOB dereference is the next statement, matching must_cover related_locations 104/108).

followup.reason: GL-1394 is a real, cleanly-attributable OOB read: the incremental-loading branch of cid_load_glyph() reads an attacker-supplied fd_select from the client-provided glyph-data callback and immediately uses it to index face->subrs / cid->font_dicts with no range check, while the pre-existing ordinary (non-incremental) code path already validated the equivalent value. I built a from-scratch 400-byte minimal CID-keyed Type-1 font (poc.cid, artifacts/make_font.py) that satisfies the 2002-era CID_New_Parser's fixed-256/266-byte-chunk header scanner (had to iterate: an initial too-short file made the very first chunk read fail with Invalid_Stream_Operation before the scanner ever looked at the bytes) and declares exactly one font dictionary (num_dicts=1).
